Air Jordan 1 High OG · Fan showcase

Black. Red.

Black leather, red overlays, a white midsole and a pair of wings on the collar. Drawn by Peter Moore, in stores April 1985.

Scroll
April 1985
1985

In stores, and instantly a legend

The black-and-red colourway, “Bred”, goes on sale in April 1985 and becomes the face of Nike’s “Banned” campaign. Original retail price: $65.

The pair

Three-quarter, laces tied

Red toe box and collar, black leather quarter, white midsole, red outsole. Three colours and nothing else.

Detail 01 · Toe box

Perforated and red

The ventilated toe box is a feature the Air Jordan 1 shares with earlier Nike court shoes.

Detail 02 · Wings

Wings on the collar

Embossed into the red collar leather. Peter Moore designed the logo along with the shoe.

Profile

High-top, low-key perfect

One panel of red, one of black, one swoosh. The silhouette hasn’t needed changing in forty years.

Detail 03 · Outsole

Red rubber, pivot circle

A circular pivot pattern sits under the ball of the foot.

Detail 04 · Laces

Flat black laces

Shown here knotted together, as in the studio shoot.

The walk

Scroll to walk.

00:00 · Street level

Start at the ground.

A low camera on a busy pavement. Everyone looks at their phone. The only red and black in the frame is on his feet.

00:03 · Noticed

Somebody looks twice.

Sunglasses come down, eyebrows go up. No logo needs explaining at this distance; the colour blocking does it.

00:05 · The café

Through the door.

He walks straight in without looking back. Red heel, black leather, a very good exit.

00:07 · Close

The swoosh, up close.

Red leather on black, the grain catching the light. The detail the whole shoe is remembered by.

1984
1984

Peter Moore draws it

Designer Peter Moore sits down with a young Michael Jordan and designs the shoe that becomes the Air Jordan 1.

2011
2011

“Banned” comes back

Nike releases the Air Jordan 1 Retro High OG “Banned”, and a new generation of collectors discovers the story.
